The N.I.C.E. process keeps the user and the evidence in view from the first question to the next version.

![The N.I.C.E. design process grows from a clearly described situation through Needs, Inquiry, Create and Communicate, and Evaluate. The cycle repeats as evidence improves the design.](../../assets/nice-design-process/lighthouse-garden.png){fig-alt="A lighthouse garden illustration shows the N.I.C.E. design cycle repeating upward from a rock labelled Situation."}

## What you will learn

- describe the situation without mixing facts, assumptions, and interpretations;
- identify the user's needs, necessities, and priorities;
- investigate several ideas before choosing one;
- communicate an idea clearly enough to receive useful feedback; and
- evaluate evidence, improve the design, and begin the next cycle.

## Lessons

::: {.ter-path-grid}
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 1. Situation

Separate facts, assumptions, and interpretations before naming the problem.

[Open the lesson](01-situation.qmd)
:::
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 2. User Needs

Describe what the user is trying to do without choosing the product first.

[Open the lesson](02-user-needs.qmd)
:::
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 3. Necessities & Nice-to-Haves

Separate what must work from what would improve the design.

[Open the lesson](03-necessities-nice-to-haves.qmd)
:::
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 4. Rank the Priorities

Score the nice-to-haves so the most useful improvements guide the design.

[Open the lesson](04-rank-priorities.qmd)
:::
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 5. Investigate & Inquire

Brainstorm, study existing ideas, ask useful questions, and choose what to test.

[Open the lesson](05-investigate-inquire.qmd)
:::
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 6. Create & Communicate

Show the idea, pitch it clearly, and ask for specific feedback.

[Open the lesson](06-create-communicate.qmd)
:::
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 7. Evaluate & Repeat

Compare the evidence with the situation and priorities, then improve the next version.

[Open the lesson](07-evaluate-repeat.qmd)
:::
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 8. Supply Chain & Life Cycle

Follow materials, making, use, repair, and end-of-life decisions beyond the first prototype.

[Open the lesson](08-supply-chain-life-cycle.qmd)
:::
:::
